## Before the first afternoon — allow 30 minutes

Install R and RStudio Desktop using the course's computer-room or personal-computer instructions.
R runs calculations; RStudio is the interface. Unzip the complete student project into a folder
you can write to. Double-click `Statistics_lab.Rproj`. Do not open files inside the ZIP.

In RStudio's **Console**, install the tutorial packages once (internet needed):

```r
install.packages(c("learnr", "shiny", "rmarkdown", "knitr", "jsonlite"))
```

Then launch from the project root:

```r
source("scripts/run_pilot.R")
```

The tutorial opens in a browser while R stays busy serving it. Type exercise code in the
tutorial's code editors; type prose in its labelled answer boxes. Click Run Code to experiment,
and Submit Answer after final edits. Download before reloading or stopping the tutorial.
Use RStudio's Stop button or Esc to stop it when finished.

## Your notebook and the Console

After the tutorial, save your download in `notebooks/` and open it in RStudio. The Source
editor contains saved code and prose. The Console shows execution and error messages;
objects in the Environment are temporary. A command typed only in the Console is not added
to your notebook. Use the chunk's green triangle to run a whole chunk. Use Ctrl+Enter on
Windows/Linux or Cmd+Enter on Mac to run the current line.

Knit reruns the saved notebook in a fresh R session. Run from the first setup chunk;
do not rely on objects left in the Environment. If the Console shows `+`, press Esc and
repair the incomplete command in your notebook. Retain the chunk markers around code,
and put explanations outside them. R names are case-sensitive.

## Troubleshooting

- “No package called ...”: install that named package, then retry.
- “Cannot open file data/...”: open the project first; keep the folder layout intact.
- Port already in use: stop the other tutorial, or run `options(course.port=8766)` before launching.
- Blank or failed launch: read the first Console error and ask the instructor; the static preview remains available.
- Rendering needs Pandoc: launch from RStudio, which supplies it.

The code engine runs locally. The student ZIP includes all teaching data; internet is not
needed after package installation. Downloaded notebooks retain submitted code and current prose,
not unsubmitted edits. Shared computers: download your work, then use Start Over for the next user.
